la:noun:labor.html:
lābor, lapsus (
inf. parag. labier, ; part. labundus, Att. ap. ; Trag. Fragm. v. 570 Rib.), 3, v. dep. n. [cf. lăbo; Sanscr. lamb- (ramb-), to glide, fall], to move gently along a smooth surface, to fall, slide; to slide, slip, or glide down, to fall down, to sink as the beginning of a fall; constr. absol., or with ad, in, inter, per, sub, super, ab, de, ex, or with abl. alone.
Lit.
In gen.
Of living beings: non squamoso labuntur ventre cerastae,per sinus crebros et magna volumina labens,: pigraque labatur circa donaria serpens,: ille inter vestes et levia pectora lapsus volvitur,: (angues) in diversum lapsi, Jul. .—Of floating: ut rate felice pacata per aequora labar,: dum Stygio gurgite labor,: tua labens navita aqua, (3, 21), 8.—Of flying: tollunt se celeres, liquidumque per aera lapsae,: vade, age, nate, voca Zephyros et labere pennis,: pennis lapsa per auras,: labere, nympha, polo,.—Of sinking, slipping down: labor, io! cara lumina conde manu,: labitur infelix (equus),; cf. : labitur exsanguis,; : super terram,: equo,: temone,

limite, : in vulnera,: in colla mariti,: alieno vulnere,: in rivo,: pondere lapsi pectoris arma sonant,.— Of gliding upwards: celeri fuga sub sidera,.—

Of things: splendida signa videntur labier,; : umor in genas Furtim labitur,: stellas Praecipites caelo labi,: perque genas lacrimae labuntur,; : lapsi de fontibus amnes,; cf.: catenae lapsae lacertis sponte sua,: lapsuram domum subire,about to tumble down,; ; cf. with cado: multa in silvis Lapsa cadunt folia,: ipsaque in Oceanum sidera lapsa cadunt,lapsis repente saxis,: ab arbore ramus,.—Of the eyes, to fall, close: labentes, oculos condere,: lumina,; ; .—
Transf.
To glide away, glide along, slip or haste away: labitur uncta carina: volat super impetus undas, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 379 Vahl.); so id. ap. (Ann. v. 476 Vahl.); cf.: labitur uncta vadis abies,; : sidera, quae vaga et mutabili ratione labuntur,.—Esp., of a transition in discourse, to pass: a dispositione ad elocutionis praecepta labor,.—
To slip away, escape: lapsus custodiā,; : e manibus custodientium lapsus,; ; .—
Trop.
In gen., to come or go gently or insensibly, to glide, glide or pass away: ilico res foras labitur,: brevitate et celeritate syllabarum labi putat verba proclivius,; : sed labor longius, ad propositum revertor,; : labitur occulte fallitque volubilis aetas,: labi somnum sensit in artus,: nostro illius labatur pectore vultus,.—
In partic.
Of speech, to die away, be lost, not be heard (very rare): ne adjectae voces laberentur atque errarent,; cf. .—
Of time, to glide, pass away, elapse: eheu fugaces labuntur anni,: anni tacite labentis origo,: labentia tempora,; ; : aetas labitur,; cf.: labente officio, when the attendance or service is ended, .—
Pregn., to sink, incline, begin to fall, go to ruin, perish: quantis opibus, quibus de rebus lapsa fortuna accidat, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 396 Vahl.); cf.: cetera nasci, occidere, fluere, labi,: labentem et prope cadentem rem publicam fulcire,: equitem Romanum labentem excepit, fulsit, sustinuit,; : sustinuit labentem aciem Antonius,: vidi labentes acies,eo citius lapsa res est,: mores lapsi sunt, id. praef.; : fides lapsa,: labentur opes,will be lost,: res,: hereditas lapsa est,.—
To slip or fall away from a thing, to lose it: hac spe lapsus, deceived or disappointed in this hope, : hoc munere,: facultatibus,to lose one's property, become poor,; : mente,to lose one's senses, go mad,; ; cf.: lapsae mentis error,.—Hence, lapsus, a, um, ruined, unfortunate, . —
To fall into or upon, to come or turn to: labor eo, ut assentiar Epicuro,; : ad opinionem,: in adulationem,: in gaudia,: in vitium,.—
To fall into error, to be mistaken, to err, mistake, commit a fault: labi, errare, nescire, decipi et malum et turpe ducimus,: in aliqua re labi et cadere,: in minimis tenuissimisque rebus,; : lapsus est per errorem suum,: consilio, ... casu,: propter inprudentiam,: in officio,: in verbo,: ne verbo quidem labi,: it vera ratione,, 176.—
Esp., to fall away from the true faith, to become apostate (eccl. Lat.): lapsorum fratrum petulantia,

to eclipse (said of the sun or moon)
la:verb:laboro.html:
lăbōro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.
[2. labor].
Neutr., to labor, take pains, exert one's self, strive.
In gen.: ne labora,: sese (aratores) sibi, laborare,: quid ego laboravi, aut quid egi, aut in quo evigilaverunt curae et cogitationes meae, si? etc.,: ne familiares, si scuta ipsi ferrent, laborarent,: si mea res esset, non magis laborarem,; : qui non satis laborarunt,: frustra laborabimus,; cf.: frustra laboret Ausus idem,: in enodandis nominibus,to exert one's self in vain,: circa memoriam et pronuntiationem,: circa nomina rerum ambitiose,: in famam, Sen. de Ira, 3, 41, 3: in commune,; : in spem,.—With dat., to toil for, to serve: cui (Jovi) tertia regna laborant,.—With in and abl.: quid est, in quo se laborasse dicit?: qua in re mihi non arbitror diu laborandum,: in dura humo,: in remigando,: in omni gente,in behalf of,.—With pro: pro hoc (L. Flacco) laborant,: pro salute mea,: pro Sestio,.—With ut: laborabat, ut reliquas civitates adjungeret,: ut honore dignus essem, maxime semper laboravi,: ut vos decerneretis laboravi,: neque te ut miretur turba labores,. —With ne: et sponsio illa ne fieret, laborasti,: quae ego ne frustra subierim ... laboro, Lent. ap. .—With inf.: quem perspexisse laborant,: amarique ab eo laboravi,; : si sociis fidelissimis prospicere non laboratis,: quod audiri non laborarit,: hunc superare laboret,; : ne quaerere quidem de tanta re laborarint,: describere,.—
In partic.
To suffer, to labor under, to be oppressed, afflicted, or troubled with.
Absol.: aliud est dolere, aliud laborare. Cum varices secabantur C. Mario, dolebat: cum aestu magno ducebat agmen, laborabat. Est inter haec tamen quaedam similitudo: consuetudo enim laborum perpessionem dolorum efficiet faciliorem, Cic.

Tusc. 2, 15, 35: valetudo tua me valde conturbat: significant enim tuae litterae, te prorsus laborare,: cum sine febri laborassem,: eum graviter esse aegrum, quod vehementer ejus artus laborarent,.—

With ex: ex intestinis,: ex pedibus,: ex renibus,: e dolore,.—Esp. of mental disorders, etc.: ex invidia,; : ex desiderio,: ex inscitia,: ex aere alieno laborare,to be oppressed with debt,.—
With ab: a re frumentaria,: ab avaritia,.—
With abl.: laborantes utero puellae,: domesticā crudelitate,: nec vero quisquam stultus non horum morborum aliquo laborat,: odio apud hostes, contemptu inter socios,: pestilentiā laboratum est,: crimine temeritatis,.—
To grieve, be in trouble, be vexed, to be concerned, solicitous, or anxious: animo laborabat, ut reliquas civitates adjungeret,: ut vos decerneretis, laboravi,: nihil laboro, nisi ut salvus sis,: sponsio illa ne fieret laborasti,.— With de (esp. of events or persons on whose account one is concerned): sororem de fratrum morte laborantem,: de quibus ego ante laborabam, ne, etc.,: laboro, ut non minimum hac mea commendatione se consecutum videretur,: noli putare me de ulla re magis laborare,: his de rebus eo magis laboro, quod, etc.,: in uno,i. e. to love,: non laboro, nihil laboro, I don't trouble myself about it, it concerns me not: cujus manu sit percussus, non laboro,: quorsum recidat responsum tuum non magnopere laboro,: Tironi prospicit, de se nihil laborat,: quid est quod de iis laborat,; .—With abl.: tuā causā,: neglegens ne qua populus laborat,.—With in: in re familiari valde laboramus,.—
To be in distress, difficulty, or danger: quos laborantes conspexerat iis subsidia submittebat,: suis laborantibus succurrere,; : ne legatus laborantibus suis auxilio foret,; .—Impers. pass.: maxime ad superiores munitiones laboratur,.—Of inanim. things: ut utraeque (triremes) ex concursu laborarent,: nec cur fraternis luna laboret equis (of an eclipse of the moon, because the sun's light is then withdrawn from it), (3, 32, 48 M.); so, luna laboret,: cum luna laborare non creditur,: laboranti succurrere lunae,: Aquilonibus Querceta laborant,: laborantem ratem deserere,: laborat carmen in fine,.—
Act. (only since the Aug. per.; for in , elaboratus is the correct reading).
To work out, elaborate, to form, make, prepare: noctibus hibernis castrensia pensa laboro,: quale non perfectius Meae laborarint manus,: arte laboratae vestes,: laborata Ceres,bread,: et nobis et equis letum commune laboras,preparest,.—
To labor at, to cultivate: frumenta ceterosque fructus,.

la:verb:labo.html:
lăbo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n.
from the same root as 1. labor
,
to totter, be ready to fall, begin to sink, to give way, be loosened (syn.: vacillo, titubo, nato).
Lit.: labat, labuntur saxa, caementae cadunt, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 142 Vahl.): signum labat,: si ex ictu ... labant dentes,: labat ariete crebro Janua,: labant curvae naves,roll,: pressaeque labant sub gurgite turres,: (turris) qua summa labantis Juncturas tabulata dabant,: littera labat,written with a trembling hand,: labare sermone,to stutter, speak indistinctly,: si labat oculus et hac atque illac movetur,is unsteady,: tarda trementi genua labant,sink,; so, pedes,: vincla labant,are loosed,.—Poet., of dying persons: inde labant populi,fall, sink,; cf.: omnia tum vero vitaï claustra lababant,.—With Gr. acc.: egressi labant vestigia prima, Forbig. (Rib. egressisque).—
Trop.
To waver, to be unstable, undecided, to hesitate (in opinion, resolution, etc.): si res labat, Itidem amici collabascunt,; cf.: scito, labare meum consilium illud, quod satis jam fixum videbatur,: labamus mutamusque sententiam,: cum ei labare M. Antonius videretur,: animumque labantem inpulit,: labantia corda,: socii labant,waver in fidelity,; cf.: fides sociorum,: animus regis,; : quīs lababat fides,whose fidelity was wavering,: mens,: tu mente labantem dirige me,: ex nimia matrem pietate labare sensit,: memoria labat,becomes weak,; cf.: mens in illis (phreneticis) labat, in hoc (cordiaco) constat,: nec dubium habebatur labare hostes,: labante jam Agrippina,: labantem ordinem contirmare,: acies labantes restituere,: sustinere labantem aciem,; .—
To sink, fall to pieces, go to ruin: quid non sic aliud ex alio nectitur, ut non, si unam litteram moveris, labent omnia?: omnes rei publicae partes aegras et labantes sanare et confirmare,; cf.: sustinuisse labantem fortunam populi Romani,: sicuti populo Romano sua fortuna labet,: labante egregia quondam disciplina,: cum res Trojana labaret,: labantibus Vitellii rebus,: si quid in moribus labaret,.

la:verb:labefacto.html:
lăbĕfacto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. freq. a.
id.
,
to cause to totter, to shake, to overthrow (syn.: quatio, concutio).
Lit.: signum vectibus,: horrea bellicis machinis,: aedium fundamenta, Cod. Th. 10, 19, 14: phalangii morsus genua labefactat,.—
Transf., in gen., to injure, weaken, ruin, destroy: sensus,: onus gravidi ventris,to procure an abortion,: colla boum,to hurt, gall,.—
Trop., to shake, throw down, overthrow, destroy, ruin, weaken (a favorite expression of Cic.): animam,: aliquem,; ; : alicujus consulatum,: alicujus dignitatem,: invidiā verbi orationem,: Aristoteles primus species labefactavit, quas mirifice Plato erat amplexatus,: conjurationem,: causam ad judicem,: fidem,: opinionem,; so, labefactare alone, to shake in purpose, move, cause to yield: me video ab ea astute labefactarier,: labefacto paulatim (sc. eum),: non illam rarae labefactes munere vestis,corrupt,, cf.: castimoniam viduae, Cod. Th. 9, 25, 1: rem publicam,: maximas res publicas ab adulescentibus labefactatas ... reperietis,; cf.: Carthaginem et Corinthum,: labefactarat

vehementer aratores superior annus, : amicitiam aut justitiam labefactare atque pervertere,: leges ac jura,: alicujus fidem pretio,: provinciarum fidem,: (praecepta) labefactari aliqua parte,.

la:adj:laboriosus.html:
lăbōrĭōsus, a, um, adj.
2. labor
,
full of labor, laborious.
Attended with much labor, laborious, toilsome, wearisome, difficult, troublesome (syn. operosus): deambulatio,: nihil laboriosius,: operum longe maximum ac laboriosissimum,: si qua laboriosa est (fabula), ad me curritur, difficult to put on the stage, opp. lenis, .—
Transf.
Inclined to labor, laborious, industrious, for the Gr. φιλόπονος (syn.: impiger, industrius): homines,: bos laboriosissimus hominis socius in agricultura, § 7.—
That undergoes much trouble and hardship, troubled, harassed: quid enim nobis duobus laboriosius?; .—Hence, adv.: lăbōrĭōsē, laboriously, wearisomely, with difficulty, ; ; .—Comp., .—Sup.: laboriosissime,;

la:noun:labes.html:
lābes, is (abl. labi for labe, ), f.
1. lābor
,
a fall, falling down, sinking in.
Lit. (rare but class.): dare labem,: motus terrae Rhodum ... gravi ruinarum labe concussit,: tantos terrae motus in Italia factos esse, ut multis locis labes factae sint terraeque desederint,subsidences of the earth,; cf.: labes agri,: terrae,; so absol.: si labes facta sit, omnemque fructum tulerit,: labes imbris e caelo,.—
Transf.
A fall, stroke, ruin, destruction: hinc mihi prima mali labes,the first blow of misfortune,: haec prima mali labes, hoc initium impendentis ruinae fuit,: metuo legionibu' labem, Enn. ap. P. (Ann. v. 283 Vahl.): quanta pernis pestis veniet, quanta labes larido,: innocentiae labes ac ruina,: labes in tabella,: regnorum labes,.—
Meton., ruin, destruction; of a dangerous person, one who causes ruin: (Verres) labes atque pernicies provinciae Siciliae,: labes popli, Plant. .—Of a bad law: labes atque eluvies civitatis,.—
In partic., the falling sickness, epilepsy, .— Hence, in gen.,disease, sickness,.

lăbĕfăcĭo, fēci, factum (labefactarier, ), 3,
v. a.; pass.: lăbĕfīo, factus, fieri
labo-facio
, to cause to totter, to shake, loosen, to make ready to fall (Cic. uses only labefactus).
Lit.: dentes alicui,: partem muri,: labefactae aedes,: labefacta ictibus arbor Corruit,; : charta (i. e. epistola) a vinclis non labefacta suis,loosened, opened,: munimenta incussu arietis labefieri,.—Poet.: ignes labefacti aëre multo,weakened,: membra voluptatis dum vi labefacta liquescunt,: calor labefacta per ossa cucurrit,.—

To cause to waver, to shake a person in his mind, principles, or fidelity: aliquem, Laber. ap. : quem nulla umquam vis, nullae minae, nulla invidia labefecit,. primores classiariorum, to shake their fidelity, excite them to mutiny, : sic animus vario labefactus vulnere nutat,; cf. in Greek construction: magno animum labefactus amore,shaken, disquieted,. —
To shake, weaken; to overthrow, ruin, destroy: haec (res publica) jam labefacta,: quo, per contumeliam consulum, jura plebis labefacta essent,: nihil hunc amicitia Sejani, sed labefacit haud minus ad exitia Macronis odium, (35): si priorem aetate et jam labefactum demovisset,: ne quis contagione ceteros labefaciat,; cf. : fidem, to shake or weaken one's credit, .
